entry.title: Edge 79+ only partially supports `list-item` in `counter-reset`
entry.content:
Summary

Edge 79+ has the same ::marker bug as Chrome for counter-reset: list-item, but the Edge entry still says full support from Edge 12. As noted in the issue, mirroring can't carry Chrome's partial flag over because Edge has its own EdgeHTML data, so this PR copies it by hand: Edge 79+ gets Chrome's partial_implementation statement and note, and the existing Edge 12 statement now ends at 79. api.PointerEvent.pointerType.fractional_coordinates already uses this same two-statement shape for Edge.

Test results and supporting details

I tested in Edge 153.0.4234.32 (Windows, headless) with this page:

<style>
  li::after { content: " [counter(list-item) = " counter(list-item) "]"; }
</style>
<ol style="counter-reset: list-item 4">
  <li>first</li><li>second</li><li>third</li>
</ol>
<ul style="list-style-type: decimal; counter-reset: list-item 4">
  <li>first</li><li>second</li><li>third</li>
</ul>

Both lists render markers 1. 2. 3., while counter(list-item) in ::after reads 5, 6 and 7. So the counter itself is reset, but the generated marker ignores the reset. This matches the existing Chrome note and crbug.com/338233131.

I didn't test EdgeHTML, so the Edge 12–79 statement keeps the support it had before and only gains version_removed: "79".

node lint/lint.js css/properties/counter-reset.json, prettier --check and the unit tests (339/339) pass.

Related issues

Fixes #30423

entry.title: Permissions-Policy: unload
entry.content:
Summary

Adds http.headers.Permissions-Policy.unload, the directive that controls whether a document can run unload event handlers. The MDN page for it landed in mdn/content#45681, and chrisdavidmills asked for the BCD entry in his approval.

Test results and supporting details

Chrome 118. chromestatus (5760325231050752) lists 115, but in 115–117 the feature was only enabled for part of stable users through a field trial:

  • 2dc337f: origin trial and experimental flag (Chrome 107).
  • 1b7f030: field trial config added.
  • 8665990 "Set PermissionsPolicyUnload to enabled for stable" ("This has been at 50/50 in stable for a while"). Chromium Dash shows this first shipped in stable in 118.0.5993.48.

Like in #23267, I used the version where it became enabled by default. The origin trial and flag aren't recorded.

Firefox and Safari: not supported. Firefox doesn't support the Permissions-Policy header. WebKit's PermissionsPolicy.cpp has no unload token.

Status. No spec_url, and standard_track: false, because the spec change (whatwg/html#7915) was never merged. experimental: true matches the MDN page and #30247 (clipboard-read/clipboard-write). Happy to change it to false if the two-year guideline should apply here.

No mdn_url yet. The page merged after the latest @ddbeck/mdn-content-inventory release, so the linter removes the URL for now. It should be added by the next inventory update.

Tested in Chromium 151: document.featurePolicy.features() includes unload, and a page served with Permissions-Policy: unload=() returns false for document.featurePolicy.allowsFeature('unload'). npm test passes.

AI disclosure: I used an AI assistant (Claude) to help research and draft this change. I reviewed the data and verified it against the sources above.

Related issues

Relates to #24843
Follow-up to mdn/content#45681

entry.title: Chrome 144 supports Temporal constructors
entry.content:
Summary

Chrome 144 shipped Temporal, and BCD already records 144 for every Temporal class, but six constructor subfeatures (Instant(), PlainDate(), PlainDateTime(), PlainMonthDay(), PlainYearMonth(), ZonedDateTime()) were left at version_added: false. This sets them to 144 (like Duration() and PlainTime()) and sets experimental to false to match their parent classes (two engines: Chrome 144, Firefox 139).

Test results and supporting details

The constructors are the class objects themselves, so they can't be unsupported while the class is supported. The false values come from the collector: bcd.testConstructor() calls new X() with no arguments, these six constructors have required parameters, and the errors they throw aren't in the harness's "needs more arguments" list, so the result was null and never updated BCD. The two constructors with only optional parameters (Duration, PlainTime) passed and already say 144.

  • mdn-bcd-results, Chrome 144 (10.20.10-chrome-144.0.0.0-windows-10-6e24cc4bf8.json): javascript.builtins.Temporal.PlainDate.PlainDate → null, "threw RangeError: Temporal error: Expected finite integer." (same for PlainDateTime / PlainMonthDay / PlainYearMonth); Instant.Instant and ZonedDateTime.ZonedDateTime → null, "threw TypeError: Cannot convert undefined to a BigInt"; the classes themselves are true.
  • mdn-bcd-results, Chrome 143: javascript.builtins.Temporal → false, so 144 is the right version.
  • ChromeStatus: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5668291307634688 (shipped in 144, desktop and Android).
  • Tested in Chrome 152 and Edge 153 (headless); all six constructors work with valid arguments:
new Temporal.Instant(0n)                       → 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
new Temporal.PlainDate(2021, 7, 1)             → 2021-07-01
new Temporal.PlainDateTime(2021, 7, 1, 12, 30) → 2021-07-01T12:30:00
new Temporal.PlainMonthDay(7, 1)               → 07-01
new Temporal.PlainYearMonth(2021, 7)           → 2021-07
new Temporal.ZonedDateTime(0n, "UTC")          → 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00[UTC]
new Temporal.PlainDate()                       → throws RangeError

Safari isn't changed here: the PlainDate / PlainDateTime / PlainMonthDay / PlainYearMonth constructors probably have the same collector artifact for Safari TP, but I can't test Safari Technology Preview.

npm run lint, npm run format and the unit tests pass locally.

Related issues

Part of #30506 (Chrome part; Safari not addressed)

entry.title: Clipboard.write() - only supports writing one ClipboardItem on Chrome/FF
entry.content:
Chrome and FF only support writing one ClipboardItem - tested using (async (i = (t) => new ClipboardItem({ "text/plain": t })) => navigator.clipboard.write([i("a"), i("b")]).then(() => "resolved", (e) => ${e.name}: ${e.message}))().
Safari allows writing as many as you like.

The spec says that you may write more than one item if the OS supports it but that if not only the first item may be writen.

But what happens on Chrome/FF is a NotAllowedError exception - the spec says that additional items should be ignored.

(async (i = (t) => new ClipboardItem({ "text/plain": t })) => navigator.clipboard.write([i("a"), i("b")]).then(() => "resolved", (e) => `${e.name}: ${e.message}`))()

Promise { <state>: "fulfilled", <value>: "NotAllowedError: Clipboard write is only supported with one ClipboardItem at the moment" }

I added this as a note, but wondering if it should be a subfeature or this is OK? (or something else)

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#45430

entry.title: Remove obsolete CSS features and enable obsolescence lint for CSS
entry.content:
Summary

Right now, our irrelevance guideline is not applied to the css/ folder because the lint has been disabled (from the start when we first implemented this rule, there were just too many data points to clean up at the time). We're now down to 25 entries there and I think it is time to finally enable this lint for CSS, too.

If you enable the lint on main you get the following messages:
